c.tagline: Malaysia's vibrant southern gateway to Singapore.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpocketing and bag-snatching in the older downtown lanes around JB Sentral and the city centre at night, and use official taxis or ride-hailing rather than touts at the causeway.

hood_desc: Johor Bahru City Centre is the dense downtown hub around JB Sentral and City Square malls, best for travellers who want to be steps from the Singapore Causeway, shopping, street food and cross-border convenience.

Iskandar Puteri is a modern, planned township with LEGOLAND, Puteri Harbour marina and corporate campuses, suited to families and business travellers wanting newer, spacious, resort-style surroundings away from the city crush.

Danga Bay is a waterfront leisure and residential strip with a promenade, seafood restaurants and high-rise condos, good for visitors who want relaxed bayfront views and evening strolls close to the city.
Tebrau is a sprawling commercial and retail belt anchored by large malls like IKEA and Toppen, ideal for shoppers, road-trippers with a car and budget-minded travellers staying near the highway.

Skudai is a university and suburban district near UTM, practical and affordable with local eateries, appealing to students, longer-stay visitors and those wanting a quieter residential base close to the airport.

water.note: Water is treated at the plant, but aging pipes make boiling or filtering advisable before drinking.

transit.pay: Tap a ManjaLink or Touch 'n Go card (sold at bus counters and convenience stores) or pay cash on board; some routes also accept contactless bank cards. Local BAS.MY routes are a flat RM1 (~$0.25), while other Causeway Link routes run RM1-4 (~$0.25-1).
transit.hours: Buses generally run 6am-11pm, with cross-border services to Singapore continuing into the early morning.
transit.note: The Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link rail line is still under construction, targeted for December 2026 - not running yet.

transit.m: Causeway Link Senai Airport Shuttle Bus (AA1) to JB Sentral, ~45-60 min

tip.r: not expected; service charge often added

landmarks: Sultan Abu Bakar State Mosque
Johor's magnificent state mosque, completed in 1900, fuses Victorian and Moorish architecture on a hilltop with sweeping views over the Straits of Johor.
Istana Besar (Grand Palace) and Royal Abu Bakar Museum
The 1866 royal palace's blue-roofed halls and manicured gardens display the Johor sultanate's dazzling regalia, gifts and hunting trophies.
Arulmigu Sri Rajakaliamman Glass Temple
A one-of-a-kind Hindu temple sheathed in over 300,000 pieces of colored glass, its mirrored sanctum shimmering like a kaleidoscopic jewel box.
Johor Bahru Old Chinese Temple
An 1870s temple uniting five Chinese dialect-group deities under one smoke-blackened roof, focal point of the spectacular annual Chingay parade.
Jalan Tan Hiok Nee Heritage Street
The atmospheric heart of old JB, where prewar shophouses serve legendary banana cakes, kopi and street art along a walkable heritage trail.
Bangunan Sultan Ibrahim
A stately 1940 tower blending Malay and colonial architecture on Bukit Timbalan, long Johor's administrative seat and the city skyline's grand dame.
Chinese Heritage Museum
A polished museum on the heritage street chronicling how five Chinese clans shaped Johor through gambier plantations, kangchu river settlements and commerce.
Danga Bay
JB's waterfront leisure strip along the Straits of Johor, with seafood restaurants, a marina and evening funfairs facing the Singapore skyline glow.
Johor Zoo (Zoo Johor)
Established in 1928 by the sultan, one of Southeast Asia's oldest zoos offers a nostalgic lakeside stroll among elephants, flamingos and orangutans.
Hutan Bandar Recreational Park (City Forest)
A pocket of tropical rainforest with seven lakes tucked inside the city centre, its shaded trails and boardwalks offering a quiet escape steps from the traffic.

train.note: The KTM Shuttle Tebrau links JB Sentral to Woodlands in Singapore in about 5 minutes — tickets sell out fast, so book early on the KTMB site. From JB Sentral, KTM ETS electric trains run north to Kuala Lumpur, Ipoh and Butterworth (Penang). The new JB–Singapore RTS Link metro is slated to open around the end of 2026 / early 2027.

bus.note: Cross-border buses to Singapore run constantly from JB Sentral and Larkin terminal, using either the Causeway (Woodlands) or the Second Link (Tuas) checkpoint. Expect immigration queues at peak times. Long-distance domestic coaches also leave from Larkin.

intl.op: Berjaya Waterfront Ferry Terminal (Dolphin Ferry / Pintas)

ferry.note: International ferries to Indonesia's Riau Islands leave from the Stulang Laut (Berjaya Waterfront) terminal to Batam Centre, Harbour Bay and Tanjung Pinang (Bintan). A second terminal at Puteri Harbour also sails to Batam and to Singapore's Tanah Merah. Bring your passport.
